newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's blue chips drive bourse higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's blue chips drive bourse higher.

text.p: Morocco's stock market ended its two-hour session higher driven by market blue chips ONA Group and Societe Nationale d'Investissemnt, brokers said.
The all-share index rose slightly 0.05 percent to 433.18 points.

"The bourse index was pulled up mainly by trading in the largest market capitalisation...Investors expect the market to continue its upward trend in the coming weeks," a stockbroker at Casablanca Finance Intermediation said.
ONA, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, rose five dirhams to close at 465 dirhams.
SNI, which has diversified stakes in more than 40 companies, gained four dirhams to close at 584 dirhams.
Cement firm Ciments de l'Oriental, continued its upward trend to close at 365 dirhams, up five dirhams over the previous session.
Steel mill Sonasid, was up two dirhams to close at 334 dirhams. The second tranche of Sonasid is expected to be privatised by end 1996.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, a market blue chip, remained unchanged at 407 dirhams.
BMCE has merged its class A and B shares into one and increased it share capital to 1.44 billion dirhams, a bourse official said on Monday.
The traded volume on the official market was estimated at 14.5 million dirhams, down from 36.9 million on Friday.
